s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent intracranial hemorrhages with hypertension and polycythemia
salient_findings: Bifrontal headaches and right-sided blurry vision
Recurrent intraparenchymal hemorrhages on CT Head
Thrombocytopenia and microcytosis on peripheral smear
key_facts: 34-year-old Thai man with history of hypertension and tobacco use disorder
Family history of polycythemia, hypertension, and stroke
Non-adherent to antihypertensive regimen
Initial presentation with blood pressures ranging from 180 to 190/80-90 mm Hg
Second presentation with systolic blood pressures 150 to 170 mm Hg
National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score of 2 due to complete left homonymous hemianopsia
Hemoglobin levels of 20.2 g/dL and 20.1 g/dL on initial and second presentations respectively
Hematocrit levels of 54.8% and 57.2% on initial and second presentations respectively
Thrombocytopenia with platelet counts of 91,000/mm³ and 76,000/mm³ on initial and second presentations respectively
Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate of 21 mm/h
Normal erythropoietin level of 7.8 mIU/mL
CT Head showing left occipital intraparenchymal hemorrhage and right posterior parietal intraparenchymal hemorrhage
MRI Brain showing no underlying masses

shortlist.label: Polycythemia vera
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated hemoglobin and hematocrit levels, family history of polycythemia

shortlist.label: Hypertensive vasculopathy
shortlist.why_kept: History of hypertension, recurrent intracranial hemorrhages

shortlist.label: Chuvash polycythemia
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated hemoglobin and hematocrit levels, possible genetic component

shortlist.label: Familial erythrocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Family history of polycythemia, elevated hemoglobin and hematocrit levels

raw.champion: Hemoglobin E-related polycythemia or Familial erythrocytosis
raw.rationale: The patient has a family history of polycythemia and elevated hemoglobin levels, with a significant proportion of Hb E and Hb Tak on hemoglobin electrophoresis, which is consistent with Hemoglobin E-related polycythemia or Familial erythrocytosis. The patient's symptoms and lab results, including high hemoglobin and hematocrit levels, thrombocytopenia, and elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate, also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Polycythemia vera
rejected.why: The patient's normal erythropoietin level and lack of other diagnostic criteria for polycythemia vera make this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Hypertensive vasculopathy
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of hypertension, the primary issue appears to be related to the hematologic abnormalities rather than hypertensive vasculopathy.

rejected.label: Chuvash polycythemia
rejected.why: There is no indication of the patient having a mutation in the VHL gene, which is typically associated with Chuvash polycythemia.

rejected.label: Essential thrombocytosis
rejected.why: The patient has thrombocytopenia rather than thrombocytosis, making this diagnosis unlikely.

gold: Compound heterozygosity for Hemoglobin Tak and Hemoglobin E with polycythemia
